topic: The Hidden Order of Chaos: Fundamental Constants and Mathematical Structure in Turbulence

sections.title: The Mystery of the Mess: Defining Turbulence
lecture_lines: Turbulence is a great mystery in physics.
Chaos seems random, but hidden structures exist.
Smooth flows break into complex, turbulent swirls.
animations: Fade in a smooth stream of horizontal blue lines (#0000FF) representing laminar flow.
Introduce a gray rock (#808080) in the path of the stream.
Transform the smooth lines into a chaotic web of white swirls (#FFFFFF) past the rock.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Gatekeeper (Reynolds Number)
lecture_lines: The Reynolds number predicts when turbulence begins.
It balances inertial forces against viscous resistance.
High inertia creates chaotic, turbulent motion.
High viscosity keeps flow smooth and steady.
Large Reynolds numbers signal a turbulent state.
animations: Show Reynolds Number formula: Re = (rho * u * L) / mu in white (#FFFFFF) at grid center.
Display a balance scale (#A9A9A9) with 'Inertia' on left and 'Viscosity' on right.
Tip the scale toward 'Inertia'; background fills with chaotic gray swirls (#D3D3D3).
Tip the scale toward 'Viscosity'; swirls transform into smooth light-blue lines (#ADD8E6).
Highlight 'Re' in formula and tip scale sharply toward 'Inertia' with turbulent background.

sections.title: The Energy Cascade: Richardson’s Russian Dolls
lecture_lines: Energy enters flow through large-scale eddies.
These large swirls fracture into smaller ones.
This process is called the energy cascade.
Big whorls have little whorls feeding on velocity.
Smaller whorls continue the chain down the scale.
animations: Draw a large rotating blue circle (#0000FF) at grid center representing a large eddy.
Split the blue circle into two medium-sized rotating yellow circles (#FFFF00).
Draw white arrows (#FFFFFF) pointing from the yellow circles to indicate further fragmentation.
Replace one yellow circle with four smaller rotating green circles (#00FF00).
Fill the remaining visual area with tiny spinning white dots (#FFFFFF) representing the smallest scales.

sections.title: The Universal Law: Kolmogorov’s -5/3 Power Scale
lecture_lines: In the inertial subrange, universal laws emerge.
Energy density follows a precise mathematical pattern.
Kolmogorov’s K41 theory describes this hidden order.
The energy spectrum decays at a -5/3 rate.
This power law reveals turbulence's mathematical heart.
animations: Create log-log axes in white (#FFFFFF) labeled E(k) and k in the visual area.
Animate a jagged white line (#FFFFFF) representing turbulence data across the graph.
Highlight the linear downward section of the data line in yellow (#FFFF00).
Overlay a clean red line (#FF0000) with a slope of -5/3 on the highlighted section.
Display and flash the label '-5/3' (#FF0000) next to the red slope line.

sections.title: The Final Stop: Kolmogorov Microscales
lecture_lines: Swirls eventually reach the Kolmogorov microscale.
Here, viscosity transforms kinetic energy into heat.
This dissipation stage ends the energy cascade.
animations: Scale down the tiny green circles until they are barely visible points.
Change the color of the points from green (#00FF00) to glowing red (#FF0000).
Fade the points into a soft red cloud representing heat dissipation.

sections.title: Universal Constants and Real-World Impact
lecture_lines: The Kolmogorov constant provides a universal scale.
This math powers weather models and aircraft design.
Order exists within the heart of chaos.
animations: Display the text 'C_K approx 0.5' in bold golden color (#FFD700).
Show a split screen with a storm swirl on the left and a plane wing on the right.
Flash the -5/3 power law formula over both images to show universality.
